chunks: And with the preceding chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, blessings of God upon both of them, that he said:

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, addressed the people at Mina and said: May God brighten the face of a servant who heard my words and heeded them, and conveyed them to those who had not heard them. For how often a carrier of knowledge is not himself a jurist, and how often does one carry knowledge to someone who is more knowledgeable than him.

Three things over which the heart of a Muslim servant will never harbour treachery: sincerity of deeds for God, sincere counsel to the leaders of the Muslims, and adherence to their community; for indeed their call encompasses and protects them from behind.
The believers are brothers; their blood is equal, and they are one hand against those other than them, and even the least of them strives to fulfil their covenant.

key_terms.إخلاص العمل: Sincerity/purity of deeds — performing actions solely for the sake of God
key_terms.تتكافأ دماؤهم: Their blood is equal — all believers have equal sanctity of life regardless of social status
key_terms.نضر الله: A prophetic supplication meaning 'may God brighten/beautify the face of' — a prayer for those who preserve and transmit knowledge
key_terms.يغل: To harbour treachery or dishonesty in one's heart; here negated, meaning the heart remains pure

ai.seo_question: What are the three things that keep a Muslim's heart pure according to the Prophet's sermon at Mina?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) delivered this sermon at Mina during the Hajj pilgrimage, urging the faithful to memorize and transmit his teachings. He identified three safeguards for a Muslim's heart: sincerity in worship, loyalty to Muslim leadership, and communal solidarity. This well-known hadith, often called 'hadith al-thalath', establishes foundational principles of Islamic communal life and the duty of knowledge transmission.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 13. And with the preceding chains of narration, from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon both, that:

The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, addressed the people at Mina, saying: "May Allah bless the servant who heard my utterances and heeded them; and conveyed to those who had not heard them. How often a person carries knowledge without he himself being learned about it, and how often does a man carry knowledge to the one who knows better than him!

There are three things over which a Mu’min’s heart will never commit a breach of the trust: Purifying the deeds solely for the sake of Allah; following the Imams of the Muslims faithfully and remaining steadfast in their groups. Their call itself protects them from all sides.
The believers are brothers to each other, defending their blood; and they act as one, single hand against the enemies. And even the smallest of them tries best to fulfil his responsibility."
